step_name: Step 10 Validation Packaging And Skill Runtime Architecture
step_goal: Define a lean HSConfig repository and repo-local Codex skill architecture that keeps `SKILL.md` short, pushes heavy detail into references and scripts, emits preview-first config packages with strict JSON validation and source provenance, and isolates guarded runtime apply from authoring and research work.

required_inputs.name: validated_upstream_contracts
required_inputs.purpose: Stable machine-readable inputs such as `deck_intake.json`, `deck_research_contract.json`, and `gameplan_contract.json` that author the config surfaces deterministically.
required_inputs.governance: Step 10 packages and validates outputs from prior contracts; it must not replace missing upstream semantics with free-form skill prose.

required_inputs.name: visionai_syntax_source_manifest
required_inputs.purpose: Pinned official-document source bundle and local cache references that define the supported runtime surfaces and syntax model.
required_inputs.governance: Every validator and packaging receipt must point back to the exact syntax source manifest used for the run.

required_inputs.name: source_citation_bundle
required_inputs.purpose: Per-claim URLs or local file refs for guide facts, card facts, runtime-surface assumptions, and packaging decisions.
required_inputs.governance: Any generated row or packaging claim without provenance must fail closed or stay in a visible suppression report.

required_inputs.name: target_surface_plan
required_inputs.purpose: Explicit declaration of which surfaces this run may generate, such as `Mulligan`, `GlobalValues`, `CardID`, or `Combo`.
required_inputs.governance: Do not infer extra files from deck archetype names or operator convenience; emit only the declared documented surfaces.

required_inputs.name: runtime_root_and_mode
required_inputs.purpose: Target runtime root plus explicit packaging mode such as `preview`, `fake`, or guarded `apply` candidate.
required_inputs.governance: Preview and fake packaging remain read-only; apply packaging is only a later guarded path and must not be activated implicitly.

required_inputs.name: fixture_and_trigger_eval_inputs
required_inputs.purpose: Representative golden decks, expected preview outputs, and trigger-evaluation prompts used to keep the skill lean and verifiable.
required_inputs.governance: Use a small curated fixture set and trigger-eval set instead of growing `SKILL.md` into a long operator manual.

produced_outputs.purpose: Short repo-local skill manifest with trigger conditions, boundaries, required inputs, output contract, and validation command.
Deferred long-form docs for operator flow, config-surface translation notes, and boundary explanations that should not load at discovery time.
Deterministic helpers for schema checks, strict JSON validation, fixture comparison, manifest generation, and package assembly.
Preview runtime files such as `Mulligan.json`, `GlobalValues.json`, per-card files, and `Combo.json` when supported by the declared surface plan.
Strict JSON and runtime-surface validation report tied to the chosen syntax model and source manifest.
Receipt covering generated preview files, hashes, suppression-report refs, source manifest refs, and `runtime_write_performed=false`.
Dry-run packaging proof that preview artifacts can be mapped into the runtime shape without touching live files.
Guarded apply evidence with runtime hashes, rollback metadata, and touched paths when and only when the dedicated apply path is invoked.
Golden examples for generated preview files, manifests, and validator receipts.
Index of fixture cases, source manifests, expected output files, and assertion policy.

reliable_uses: Keep HSConfig discoverable by loading only skill metadata at startup and deferring detailed instructions, references, and scripts until the skill is actually selected.
Separate reusable repository policy from task-specific workflow logic by keeping repo-wide rules in `AGENTS.md` and step-specific procedure in the skill and references.
Package preview outputs, fake-write evidence, and guarded-apply evidence as distinct layers with different authority and different `runtime_write_performed` expectations.
Enforce strict JSON materialization, filename-to-surface routing, row provenance, and supported-surface checks before any preview package is treated as ready.
Emit manifests and receipts that let later steps trace every generated row and every packaged file back to upstream contracts and cited sources.
Use small deterministic scripts and test fixtures for mechanical work instead of expanding the skill body with repeated command text, schema details, or large examples.
Keep runtime mutation outside the skill activation boundary by routing live writes only through the dedicated runtime writer.
limitations: This step can define packaging, validation, and skill structure, but it cannot prove that a generated deck package improves gameplay or that the live runtime accepted the files without later guarded-write evidence.
A lean skill does not replace upstream card, archetype, mulligan, combo, or global-values research contracts; it only orchestrates and validates them.
Local skill examples such as HSTuner are useful anti-bloat evidence, but they are not a normative API contract for Codex or a proof that only one workflow split is valid.
Strict preview validation can prove file shape, provenance shape, and supported-surface alignment, but it cannot by itself prove undocumented runtime semantics or hidden-information correctness.
Plugin packaging is distribution strategy, not authoring necessity; Step 10 should start repo-local and avoid plugin complexity unless cross-repo reuse is actually needed.
relevant_config_surfaces: AGENTS.md repository guidance that declares guardrails and verification expectations

aggressive_generation_policy.principle: Keep the skill small and the compiler aggressive: preserve all source-backed, documented, syntax-safe config intent in preview outputs, and move everything else into deterministic manifests, suppression reports, or deferred references instead of bloating instructions.
rules: Prefer repo-local `.agents/skills/hsconfig` authoring first, because the workflow is tightly coupled to HSConfig outputs and repository tests.
Keep `SKILL.md` limited to trigger conditions, boundaries, required inputs, output contract, validation entrypoint, and one compact example.
Move long syntax explanations, edge cases, and operator walkthroughs into `references/` so they load only when the skill is selected.
Move deck decode, schema validation, hash calculation, fixture diffing, and package assembly into `scripts/` so the skill does not narrate deterministic mechanics.
Generate all declared documented preview surfaces in one pass when upstream contracts support them; do not hold back valid surfaces just because one separate claim was suppressed.
When a claim cannot be translated safely, emit a visible suppression record or contract gap instead of weakening the claim into guessed JSON or silently dropping it.
Treat preview, fake, and guarded apply as separate packaging stages with separate receipts and validation gates, never as one implicit command with hidden mutation.

validation_gates: The research JSON itself must cover every required field in `fields.yaml` and pass `validate_json.py` for this research batch.
Generated preview files must parse as strict JSON with no comments or trailing commas.
Preview validation must reject unsupported runtime surfaces, aggregate `CardBehavior.json`, wrong top-level shapes, and invalid row provenance.
Every generated preview row must have exactly one provenance record that maps file path and JSON pointer back to a stable upstream rule and source citation.
The syntax report must include a source stamp with manifest reference, source doc keys, registry policy, and parser version or equivalent source-parser identity.
The config preview receipt must include hash coverage for generated preview files and for required suppression reports when those reports exist.
Preview and fake-stage artifacts must keep `runtime_write_performed=false`.

Guarded apply must require a separate `write_receipt.json`, same-invocation runtime snapshot, rollback metadata, source-hash freshness, and apply-mode validation before any live runtime mutation is considered ready.
Fixture comparisons must pass for at least one representative deck package and one negative or suppression case before the skill is treated as stable.
Trigger-evaluation prompts must show that the skill activates for HSConfig packaging tasks and stays inactive for unrelated Step 2 tuning or runtime-analysis tasks.
architectural_implications: HSConfig should keep the repository rule layer in `AGENTS.md` and the reusable workflow layer in `.agents/skills/hsconfig`, rather than duplicating policy blocks in every reference file.
The skill should be repo-local and minimal: `SKILL.md`, a small `references/` set, and a small `scripts/` set. Do not start with plugin packaging, cloud distribution, or multiple overlapping skills.
Add dedicated modules for preview validation, packaging receipts, manifest generation, and fixture comparison instead of burying those concerns inside one monolithic authoring script.

The CLI surface should be explicit and stage-based, for example `intake`, `research`, `compile`, `validate-preview`, `package-runtime --mode fake`, and `package-runtime --mode apply`, so preview and apply authority are visibly separated.
Source provenance should be first-class in packaging: manifests, syntax reports, preview receipts, and row-provenance tables should all preserve source IDs and file hashes.
Use one compact reference example near the skill, and move broader regression cases into `tests/fixtures/hsconfig` so maintenance happens through tests, not through a larger and larger skill body.
Do not copy HSTuner's broader session-management, post-game loop, and guarded auto-tuning surface into HSConfig. Step 10 is an authoring and packaging workflow, not a live-tuning system.
If cross-repo reuse later becomes real, package the already-lean repo-local skill as a plugin without changing the preview/apply contracts.

recommended_contracts.purpose: Deck identity, runtime root, target mode, declared surfaces, and source citation refs required for a packaging run.
Pinned URLs, local cache paths, capture dates, and hashes for official syntax docs and deck-guide evidence used during generation.
Planned output files, skipped surfaces, suppression expectations, and package stage for the current run.
Files written, file hashes, unresolved gaps, and `runtime_write_performed` state for the run.
Combined syntax, schema, provenance, receipt, and fixture-diff results for every generated surface.
Preview package receipt with report refs, preview hashes, syntax source stamp linkage, and stage authority.
Dry-run proof that the preview package can map to the live runtime layout without writing to it.
Guarded apply evidence with runtime hash checks, touched paths, rollback operations, and after-hash capture.
Golden-case index for deck fixtures, expected outputs, negative cases, and validator assertions.
Explicit, implicit, and negative prompts used to keep activation boundaries stable as the skill evolves.

never_autogenerate_without: Validated upstream deck and gameplan contracts rather than free-form deck notes alone.
A cited source manifest that covers every non-trivial strategic or syntax claim used in the package.
An explicit surface plan stating which runtime files may be generated in this run.
A successful strict-preview validation pass over every generated JSON file.
Row-provenance coverage showing exactly one source-backed provenance entry per generated runtime row.
A preview receipt and, for runtime-targeted packaging, a fake-runtime receipt before guarded apply is even considered.
At least one golden fixture or fixture-diff pass proving the packaging layout and validator outputs match a known case.
A deliberate apply invocation for live runtime mutation; preview or fake packaging alone must never imply apply authority.

Official guidance for manual trigger checks, small eval sets, and systematic skill verification.
Official source for repository instruction layering and for keeping project guidance practical and close to the code.
Official source for concise `AGENTS.md`, practical verification guidance, and keeping reusable guidance out of repeated prompts.
Primary local evidence for the preview, fake, apply, and Step 2 read-only artifact boundaries that HSConfig should emulate without inheriting Step 2 complexity.
Primary local evidence for preview-first command ordering, apply boundary, and required Step 1 validation outputs.
Primary local evidence for strict JSON parsing, runtime-surface validation, and row-provenance enforcement.
Primary local evidence for receipt checks, suppression-report linkage, source-stamp validation, and guarded-apply gate conditions.
Primary local evidence for artifact-family separation, preview authority, and the distinction between non-authoritative preview outputs and apply evidence.
